[QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الأخفش | reports | Al-Akhfash glosses khadiran as green, citing an Arabic expression about seeing a striped garment as rain-colored.
[QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Al-khaḍr is fresh green vegetable growth.

[QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Ṭalʿ is the palm spathe before it splits to reveal the bloom; the bloom is also called ṭalʿ, as is what appears on a palm cluster.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | The water was sent down from clouds or from the direction of the sky.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r10] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | Qinwān is read with ḍamma on qāf, by analogy with dhiʾb/dhuʾbān, and with fatḥa as a collective noun, since fiʿlān is not a plural pattern.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r11] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | The clusters are near enough to reach, or densely clustered close together; mentioning these alone implies their opposite and adds a mark of favor.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r12] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | Vineyards coordinate with 'the growth of every kind'; Nāfiʿ reads them nominative as a new subject with an implied predicate, but they cannot coordinate with palm clusters because grapes do not grow from palms.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r13] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | Olives and pomegranates either coordinate with the plant growth or are accusatives of specification, because these two types were prized among the audience.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r14] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | The description may modify the pomegranate or all the fruits: some resemble one another and others differ in shape, size, color, and taste.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r15] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The fruit to observe is the fruit of each of the plants just mentioned.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r16] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · حمزة والكسائي | reports | Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the tāʾ and mīm with ḍamma, treating thumur as a plural of thamarah or of thimār.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r17] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | At first fruiting, the fruit is tiny and scarcely useful; at ripening it becomes large, useful, and delicious.

[BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The pronoun refers to the water.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | This means the growth of every kind of plant and displays God's power in producing diverse varieties watered by one water, as in the cited description of crops watered by one water yet differing in taste. | mentions 13:4
[BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r5] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | The pronoun may refer either to the plant or to the water.

[BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r7] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The grain stacked in layers is grain growing from the green shoot, namely an ear of grain.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r8] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | The syntax may mean producing palms from palms, with bunches from their spathes, or producing bunches from palm spathes; alternatively min al-nakhl predicates qinwān and min ṭalʿihā is an appositive.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r9] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Qinwān are palm clusters, the plural of qinw, like ṣinwān as the plural of ṣinw.

[NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r11] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Iftʿāl and tafaʿul forms often share a meaning, as in the verbs for resembling; olives and pomegranates are each alike in some respects and unlike in others.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Ṭalʿ is the first growth emerging from a date palm within its sheaths; a palm is said to produce its ṭalʿ when it brings it out.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو عبيد | reports | Abu Ubayd says ṭalʿ is like the palm's sheath before it opens from the inner spadix, and the inner spadix itself is also called ṭalʿ.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r12] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | A قنو is a palm cluster or bunch, also called الكباسة; the term can denote the cluster's stalk.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r13] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · القرطبي | reports | Al-Qurtubi transmits another sense for قنو: the palm heart, الجمار.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r14] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The few plural is أقناء and the many plural قنوان; dialects vary between قاف vowels and replacing the plural's واو with ياء, while the singular remains قنو.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r15] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | زيتون is on the pattern فيعول like قيصوم, supported by أرض زتنة and the rarity of فعلول; its root differs from زيت.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r16] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | رمان follows فعال like حماض and عناب, not فعلان, as shown by the expression أرض رمنة.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r17] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The forms ينع, الينع, and الينوع vary by dialect and mean that fruit has ripened and matured; أينه also means it ripened.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r18] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الحجاج | reports | Al-Hajjaj's line about heads that have ripened uses أينعت metaphorically for maturity and the time to harvest.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r19] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farra says ينع and أينع can mean that fruit turned red; the liʿān hadith compares a red-born child to a red stone called الينعة, perhaps agate or a kind of it.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r20] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Some derive الينع as the plural of يانع, by analogy with تاجر/تجر and صاحب/صحب.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj takes خضر as meaning green: the analogy is أخضر/خضر as أعور/عور.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · غيره | reports | Another view derives خضر from freshness, not color; calling the world green is a metaphor for freshness, while actual greenness denotes color.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الليث | reports | Al-Layth says خضر means crops in the Qur'an, but in ordinary speech it can mean any green plant.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Tarakub describes one thing mounted or piled upon another.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | From the greenery God brings stacked grains such as wheat, barley, and legumes, and layered seeds in fruits such as pomegranates and pine nuts.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | نخرج may be an adjectival clause describing خضرا or an independent report.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | After recalling the favor of creating people, the passage recalls provision that sustains and serves their needs; here السماء means clouds.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farra says نبات means sustenance suitable as food for everything; on this reading كل شيء is restricted to what is nourished.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The shift from third-person reference to first-person plural in فأخرجنا is an iltifat, using the majestic plural.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | خضرا means fresh, lush, and tender, here emerging from the plant.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The phrase is a subject-predicate sentence; ومن طلعها is an appositional specification of ومن النخل, yielding clusters from the palm's spathes.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r13] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Presenting the palm clusters as a nominal sentence signals that this provision is established and assured.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r12] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | ثمر can include what grows on the tree, while calling the tree itself ثمر is figurative.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r13] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الجمهور؛ قتادة، الضحاك، ابن محيصن | reports | The majority read وينعه with fatḥa on yāʾ and still nūn; Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Ibn Muḥayṣin read yāʾ with ḍamma.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r14] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن أبي عبلة، اليماني، ابن محيصن | reports | Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Yamānī read يانعه, an active participle from ينع; al-Zamakhsharī attributes this reading to Ibn Muḥayṣin.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r15] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · المروزي | reports | Al-Marwazī says alternating winds expose fruit to sun and then shade, preventing both failure to ripen and scorching.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | مشتبها may be a circumstantial accusative describing the pomegranate because it is nearest, with the matching circumstance omitted after the olive.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Alternatively, مشتبهًا may describe the earlier olive by precedence, with the estimate that both olive and pomegranate are similar and dissimilar.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī’s inference from the verse of poetry: بريئًا can describe singular, dual, or plural, whereas a dual circumstantial form would be required.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjāj says olive and pomegranate are paired because Arabs know both trees have leaves extending along the branch from end to end; a poem illustrates the pairing.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Look with the eyes, as إلى indicates; the sight leads to reflection and inference about God’s power in changing fruit through its stages.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The verse singles out the beginning and ripeness, though intermediate stages invite reflection, because the endpoints are more remarkable and clearer proofs.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن وثاب، مجاهد، حمزة، الكسائي | reports | Ibn Waththāb, Mujāhid, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read ثمره with ḍamma on both letters; Ibn Waththāb and Mujāhid explain it as kinds of wealth yielded by the tree.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو علي | prefers | Abū ʿAlī prefers ثمر as a plural of ثمرة, on the pattern of خشبة and خشب, with comparable plurals from weak nouns.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | ذلكم points to everything just mentioned, from splitting grain and pit through all God created and bestowed.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Its juice is delicious, temperate, strengthening, and both food and medicine; combining opposed qualities in one fruit displays God’s power.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The signs demonstrate God’s perfect power, workmanship, and exclusive creation; they benefit only those whom God has destined to believe.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Specifying believers signals that manifest signs do not benefit those whose destiny is unbelief.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The sequence follows the earlier mention of splitting grain: vegetation is followed by stacked grain, then dates from their pits. | mentions 6:95
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Crops precede trees because grain is nourishment, fruit a delicacy, and nourishment comes first.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Date palms precede other fruits because they serve Arabs as a staple comparable to nourishment.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Grapes are first among fruits as the noblest; all their successive states and products are useful, including sour and ripe grapes, vinegar, syrup, and raisins.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Olive follows for its use as food and its highly beneficial oil for eating, lighting, and other uses.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Pomegranate is singled out for its mixture of rind, pith, seed, and juice: the first three are cold, dry, dense, and astringent, while its juice has opposite qualities.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | إلى ثمره depends on انظروا, which means to look with reflection; إلى is used because this sense includes contemplation.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r10] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | In al-Anʿām and Yāsīn, ʿĀsim, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathir, Ibn ʿAmir, and Abu ʿAmr read fatḥ; in al-Kahf, ʿĀsim reads fatḥ, the Brothers and Nāfiʿ/Ibn Kathir/Ibn ʿAmir double ḍamma, and Abu ʿAmr ḍamma with sukūn. | mentions 18:34

[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r11] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | The distinction offered for al-Kahf—ḍamma for wealth and fatḥ for edible fruit—cannot explain the readings in al-Anʿām and Yāsīn. | mentions 18:34, 36:35
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r12] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | As a parallel reading example, Abu ʿAmr, al-Kisaʾi, and Qunbul read خشب, while the others use ḍamma; the author calls the former reading analogous to the one just discussed.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الأخوان، author | reports | The Brothers' double-ḍamma reading ثمر admits four analyses: a singular noun, a plural of plurals, a plural of ثمر, or a plural of ثمرة.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | One analysis treats ثمر as a singular noun, like طنب or عنق.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Another analysis makes ثمر a plural of plurals: ثمر is plural of ثمار, itself plural of ثمرة, comparable to أكم and إكام.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A third analysis treats ثمر as a plural of ثمر, by analogy with the two plural forms أسد and أسد.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الفارسي | prefers | Al-Farisi prefers reading ثمر as the plural of ثمرة, like خشبة/خشب, أكمة/أكم, and the defective pairs لابة/لوب, ناقة/نوق, ساحة/سوح.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The majority's fatḥ reading الثمر is a collective noun whose singular is ثمرة, like شجر/شجرة, بقر/بقرة, and جزر/جزرة.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | The rare reading with a still second radical either eases the double-ḍamma reading or is a plural of ثمرة; with the latter analysis, ثمر parallels سمر and its broken plural is أثمار.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو عمرو | reports | Abu ʿAmr reads the Kahf occurrence with ḍamma and a still م; that is eloquent, though consistency would suggest using it here too, since recitation follows transmission. | mentions 18:34
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | إذا أثمر is a time adverb for انظروا, either purely temporal or conditional with an omitted or advanced response: when it fruits, look at it.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | The majority read ينعه with fatḥa on ي and sukūn on ن; Ibn Muhaysin, also reported from Qatada and al-Dahhak, uses ḍamma, while Ibrahim ibn Abi ʿAbla and al-Yamani read يانعة.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | الينع with fatḥa or ḍamma is the verbal noun of ripening; fatḥa is Hijazi and ḍamma is used by some Najdis, with variants ينَع and ينوع.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Alternatively الينع is a plural of يانع, like تاجر/تجر and صاحب/صحب; ينعت and أينعت both mean that fruit ripened, in triliteral and quadriliteral forms.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الحجاج | reports | Al-Hajjaj's phrase رؤوسا قد أينعت وحان قطافها describes heads as ripe and ready to be harvested.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farraʾ says أينعت means the fruit turned red; the hadith phrase compares a red-born child to الينعة, a red bead said to be carnelian or a kind of it.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو عبيد | reports | Abu ʿUbayd says ينعت تينع has fatḥa in the past and kasra in the present, citing a line about olives ripening; al-Layth reverses the vowels.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The close addresses believers because the signs show one God's power to create varied products from one soil and water; only reflective believers benefit from them.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | The apparent antecedent of منه is نبات; Zamakhshari gives only this option. من then marks part or point of origin.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | reports | Abu al-Baqa also allows منه to refer to ماء, with من expressing cause.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | reports | If منه refers to water, Abu al-Baqa treats the second فأخرجنا clause as a semantic replacement; al-Samin says strict grammatical بدل is not evident and prefers coordination.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | Al-Samin corrects the Shaykh: Abu al-Baqa’s بدل analysis depends on منه referring to water and cannot be attributed to the plant reading.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو إسحاق | reports | Abu Ishaq says خضر and أخضر both mean green, like عور and أعور.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Green lies between white and black but closer to black; thus black can denote green and vice versa, as in سواد العراق for its tree-covered greenness.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | مدهامتان in 55:64 means intensely black because of the gardens’ abundant moisture and greenness. | mentions 55:64
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | المخاضرة is selling green fruit before ripening; الخضيرة is a palm whose unripe dates fall while green.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · النبي | reports | The Prophet explains خضراء الدمن as a beautiful woman from a bad upbringing; الدمن are refuse heaps where attractive plants may grow.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الجمهور وابن محيصن والأعمش | reports | The majority read نخرج active in first-person plural; Ibn Muhaysin and al-Aʿmash read passive يخرج, with حب as its agent.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | On either reading, the clause is most naturally an adjective of خضرا, though it may be independent.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | متراكبا can be nominative or accusative as an adjective of حب, following the two case parses.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | Best parse: من النخل is a fronted predicate, من طلعها a partitive بدل with repeated preposition, and قنوان a delayed topic; the nominal clause coordinates with the prior verbal clause.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | On al-Akhfash’s alternative, قنوان is raised as subject by من النخل, with من طلعها as apposition.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A تنازع parse has both prepositional phrases seeking قنوان as subject: Basrans prefer the second governor and insert a pronoun in the first, Kufans the reverse.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | reports | Abu al-Baqa’s other parse makes قنوان the subject governed by من طلعها, with a pronoun in من النخل; al-Samin assigns governance to the second phrase.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A further parse makes قنوان a topic, من طلعها its predicate, and posits an understood شيء or ثمر with من النخل; al-Samin rejects it because the predicate cannot also be بدل.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | If من طلعها is already the predicate, it cannot also be بدل; taking من النخل as predicate repeats the earlier parse.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | rejects | The Shaykh calls the preceding grammatical account confused.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r10] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الواحدي | reports | Al-Wahidi compares the new final ḍamma to the distinction between منصور and the vocative حار in يا حار.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r11] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الجمهور والأعمش والحباب والأعرج | reports | The majority use qaf kasra, called Hijazi; al-Aʿmash, al-Habbab from Abu ʿAmr, and al-Aʿraj use ḍamma. Al-Farra assigns it to Qays and says kasra is more common; Ibn ʿAtiyya reverses the Hijazi label.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Zamakhshari makes قنوان a topic with its predicate omitted and inferred from أخرجنا; the Shaykh and al-Samin find this unnecessary because the clause already informs independently.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن عطية | reports | Ibn ʿAtiyya links من النخل to an omitted verb and makes من طلعها قنوان a nominal clause functioning as the object of نخرج.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | rejects | A verb taking one object cannot take a whole clause unless it licenses clausal complements and a blocker prevents governance within it; نخرج has neither condition.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | holds | If the verb governed a word inside the nominal clause, قنوان would have to be accusative as its object.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | reports | With passive يخرج, the palm clause may coordinate with the passive clause; the Shaykh prefers the alternative topic-predicate parse.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | قنوان is the broken plural of قنو, like صنوان from صنو; قنو is a date cluster or stalk, also called كباسة.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Imruʾ al-Qays uses قنو النخلة المتعثكل in a foliage simile and elsewhere uses قنوانا for red dates.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو علي | reports | Abu ʿAli says the plural’s kasra replaces rather than preserves the singular kasra of قنو, as in هجان and ظراف.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو عمرو | reports | A third form, قنوان with qaf fatḥa, is Abu ʿAmr’s reading in Harun’s transmission.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r10] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Other distinctions include dual alif changing to ya in oblique cases and its nun dropping in annexation, while plural nun remains; dual nisba drops its markers but plural قنواني retains them.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r11] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Though قنوان and صنوان resemble sound masculine plurals, broken pattern فعلان itself conveys plurality rather than two added markers.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن جني | reports | Ibn Jinni parses the fatḥa form as a collective noun, not a plural, since Arabic has no plural pattern فعلان

[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري وأبو البقاء | reports | Zamakhshari compares it with ركب, Abu al-Baqa with الباقر; al-Durr prefers الباقر because it is uncontroversially collective while ركب is disputed by Abu al-Hasan.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The fatḥa form’s analysis is supported because the singular is attested with qaf kasra or ḍamma, never fatḥa.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · تميم وربيعة | reports | Two further dialectal forms use ya rather than waw: قنيان with qaf ḍamma or kasra; both are Tamim and Rabiʿa forms.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | These dialects retain waw in the singular and never use ya there, so the plural unexpectedly differs from the singular stem.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | The view that قنو means a palm’s heart or pith is nearly mistaken: the pith is inside the palm, unlike the nearby fruit; the established meaning is a cluster.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو عبيد | reports | Abu ʿUbayd says the dual of قنو is قنوان with kasra on nun and the plural matches it, like صنو/صنوان, an otherwise unmatched form.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | In pause, dual and plural قنوان are homonyms; in connected speech, case marking distinguishes them.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الراغب | reports | Al-Raghib compares قناة to قنو because both resemble branches; a water channel is explained by its straight extension or as a place that stores water.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r10] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | جنات may instead coordinate with خضرا.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r11] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | prefers | Zamakhshari prefers taking accusative جنات as اختصاص, singling out these kinds like والمقيمي الصلاة; al-Samin says his wording implies he treats nominative as famous and accusative as anomalous.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الراغب | reports | Al-Raghib also derives قناة from قاناه, ‘mixed it’; Imruʾ al-Qays’s مقاناة البياض بصفرة supports mixture.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الراغب | reports | Nasal قنا, the curvature of a nose, is named by resemblance in shape; a man is أقنى and a woman قنواء.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | طلع is the first growth to emerge from the palm within its enclosing sheaths.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو عبيد | reports | Abu ʿUbayd defines الطلع as the kafara before it splits from agrīḍ, also called طلع; أطلعت النخلة describes the palm producing it while طلع الطلع describes the growth’s emergence.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | An unnamed poem lists palm-fruit stages: طلع, خلال, بلح, بسر, رطب, then تمر.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الجمهور | reports | The majority read جنات accusative, coordinating it with نبات: the water brings forth plants generally and gardens specifically.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | This is a specific-after-general construction honoring these kinds, like naming Gabriel and Michael after the angels and messengers. | mentions 2:98
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | On this parse, the palm clause is parenthetical and formed as a topic-predicate sentence to magnify the blessing of dates, a major Arab food combining enjoyment and sustenance.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Al-Aʿmash, Muhammad ibn Abi Layla, and Abu Bakr in a report from ʿAsim read وجنات in the nominative.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | As a nominative subject with omitted predicate, al-Zamakhshari supplies ثم, while Abu al-Baqa supplies من الكرم, matching ومن النخل.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Al-Nahhas estimates ولهم and Ibn ʿAtiyya ولكم; the omitted-predicate construction also parallels وحور عين, whose understood predicate is لهم, and is accepted by Sibawayh, al-Kisaʾi, and al-Farraʾ. | mentions 56:22
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A delayed omitted predicate can be أخرجناها, inferred from the earlier فأخرجنا; Ibn al-Anbari had already analyzed the phrase this way.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Al-Farazdaq's line raises الخمر although it is the object, understood as والخمر أحلها الطعنة, illustrating delayed coordination with an omitted predicate.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن الأنباري | rejects | Ibn al-Anbari also allows coordination on قنوان by proximity: eyes follow brows though they are not plucked, just as grape gardens do not come from palm flowers; the author calls this defense weak and characteristic of adjectival attraction.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Coordination on قنوان is also possible if من النخل does not scope over the gardens: palm clusters and separately produced grape gardens; al-Tabari gives this analysis, Ibn ʿAtiyya weakens it, and Abu al-Baqa objects that grapes do not grow from palms.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | من أعناب is an adjectival phrase modifying جنات; it is nominative with the nominative reading and accusative with the other reading, and depends on an omitted element.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | All readers have الزيتون and الرمان in the accusative; they may coordinate with جنات or with نبات, as al-Zamakhshari and Abu al-Baqa explain.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Ibn ʿAtiyya instead coordinates these two nouns with حبا; a later conjunct may attach either to the immediately preceding item or to the first item in the series.
